purpose: Teach: 東大/明治維新/封建/前例/欠落/気の毒/暴走/衝動

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、本気で、絶対、東大、絶対、史、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、感心
lines.en: Sakura, I have to say — your paper really engaged with Tokyo University level material. The depth of your research was genuinely impressive.
lines.style: Warm, steady opening. Genuine admiration — not performative. Measured pace. Lets the compliment land without rushing past it. Teacher's composed confidence.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。本気で、絶対、明治維新、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you so much. I wanted to really dig into the Meiji Restoration — to understand how deeply it shaped everything that came after. I'm grateful you pushed me to think bigger.
lines.style: Sincere and direct. No defensive edge. Meets her teacher's eye. Takes the compliment seriously without deflecting. Speaks from genuine thought, not habit.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 江戸時代の、本気で、絶対、封建、絶対、制、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、視野、広い、絶対、立派、絶対、本気で、感心
lines.en: And you didn't just skim the surface — you brought in the Edo period context, traced how the feudal system actually broke down. That kind of perspective is rare at your level.
lines.style: Slower, more reflective. Leaning slightly forward. Thinking out loud a little. The tone of someone who has read it carefully and wants her to know it. Genuine.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。歴史上の、本気で、絶対、前例、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes — I wanted to show how one era doesn't just appear out of nowhere. You have to understand what came before.
lines.style: Clear and grounded. Not trying to impress back, just answering truthfully. The earnestness beneath her cooler surface showing through. Confident but not performative.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 記録の、本気で、絶対、欠落、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: Exactly. And you handled something really difficult — the gaps in the historical record, the voices that didn't make it into documents. That's mature thinking.
lines.style: Engaged and affirming. Slight nod of recognition. The kind of teacher-voice that makes a student feel actually seen. Warm but professional. Not overdoing it.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。戦争被害者への、本気で、絶対、気の毒、絶対、な、絶対、立場、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: I tried to give space to the people who suffered — the ones whose stories weren't written down. War victims especially. It felt important to acknowledge that, even in a research paper.
lines.style: Quieter, more vulnerable. Careful with her words — this matters to her. Not defensive, just earnest. A crack showing in her sarcasm-armor. Speaks slowly, meaning each word.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦時の、本気で、絶対、暴走、絶対、論文で、絶対、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: That compassion came through. You examined how wartime pressures can push a nation to make decisions it otherwise wouldn't — without excusing them, but understanding them.
lines.style: Contemplative and balanced. Not cheerful, but honest. The tone of someone talking about something hard that matters. Steady. Respecting the seriousness of the subject.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。歴史上の、本気で、絶対、衝動、絶対、的決断、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I wanted to ask: how do good people make terrible choices? Not to excuse it, but to understand it — so maybe we recognize the signs next time.
lines.style: Measured and grave. Speaking from real thought, not parroting. A glimpse of what Sakura actually cares about beneath the sarcasm. Sincere without being naive. Ending thoughtfully.
